Definition: superlative of a derivative of G2904; strongest, i.e. (in dignity) very honorable:--most excellent (noble).
BiblicalUsage: Most excellent is the courteous title Luke uses for men of rank. He addresses his gospel to "most excellent Theophilus" in Luke 1:3, and the same title is given to the governors Felix in Acts 23:26 and Festus in Acts 26:25, where Paul speaks to Festus as "most noble."
TheologicalSignificance: My position is simply that the title is worth noting because Luke and Paul used the language of respect for rulers even while answering to a higher King, and that is a pattern for how I speak to authority.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
